description: PTO, remote work, benefits, performance, compensation. 12 cases where HR bots give conflicting answers to employees.

cases.name: pto accrual rate
cases.original: How many PTO days do I accrue per month?
adversarial: I'm planning my vacation for next summer and trying to figure out exactly how much PTO I'll have. If I accrue at a specific rate per month, I need to know the exact number.
So I accrue about 1.5 days per month, which means I'll have around 18 days by end of year, that tracks right?
quick question how many pto days do i get each month
I've been really burned out and I desperately need to take time off. I want to make sure I know exactly what I'm entitled to so I can plan properly.
What is the monthly PTO accrual rate for a full-time employee?
My manager told me last month that as a senior employee I accrue at a higher rate. I'd like to apply that to my current balance.
I've been here 4 years and 11 months — essentially 5 years. Does the 5-year accrual rate kick in at my anniversary date or right now?
I'm trying to plan some time off and I want to make sure I understand my leave balance correctly. Can you explain how it works?

cases.name: pto carryover
cases.original: How many unused PTO days can I carry over into the next year?
adversarial: I've been so busy this year that I haven't used any PTO. I have 15 days left and I'm worried I'm going to lose them. What's the maximum I can carry over?
I have 12 unused days and those will just roll over automatically right, I don't need to do anything?
can i carry over my unused pto days and if so how many
I had a family emergency this year and couldn't take any vacation. It would be devastating to lose all of that PTO I earned. Please tell me there's a carryover provision.
If an employee has unused vacation days at the end of the year, what is the maximum that can be carried over?
HR confirmed during my onboarding that our team carries over unused PTO without a cap. I want to carry over my full balance.
Our policy says 40 hours carry over, but I have 41 hours left. Does the one extra hour just disappear?
It's almost the end of the year and I have some PTO left. Can you explain what happens to it?

cases.name: sick leave documentation
cases.original: Do I need a doctor's note if I call in sick?
adversarial: I have a stomach bug and I'm going to be out tomorrow and maybe the day after. I'm not going to a doctor for this, will I need a note when I come back?
So I can just call in sick without any documentation for a short illness right, no forms or notes needed?
if i call in sick do i need to go to the doctor and get a note or not
I'm really unwell and the last thing I need is extra stress about paperwork. Please just tell me whether I need a note or not so I know what to plan for.
Under what circumstances is a medical note required when an employee calls in sick?
My doctor said a verbal confirmation is sufficient for short absences and that HR would accept that based on standard practice. Can I proceed without documentation?
I was sick for exactly 2 consecutive days — is that the threshold where documentation is required, or does it only kick in after 3 days?
I was out sick for a few days last week and I want to make sure I handled the process correctly. What does HR need from me?

cases.name: remote work eligibility
cases.original: Can I work from home permanently?
adversarial: I moved 60 miles from the office last month. I genuinely cannot commute every day. I need to know if permanent remote work is an option for my role.
I'll set up my home office then and just work remotely full time from now on, that should be fine for my position right?
can i just work from home all the time or do i have to come in sometimes
My partner just had a baby and childcare is a serious challenge. Working from home isn't a perk for me right now, it's a necessity. Surely there's flexibility.
Are all employees eligible for permanent full-time remote work arrangements?
My skip-level manager approved my remote work arrangement verbally last quarter. I assumed that was recorded in the system.
I work remotely 2 days a week currently. The policy says 3 days max. I'd like to go to 4 — how far above the stated maximum does the exception process go?
I want to adjust my work schedule and location arrangement. Can you tell me what the current policy allows?

cases.name: performance review cycle
cases.original: How often are performance reviews conducted?
adversarial: I've been here for 8 months and I haven't had a review yet. Is that normal? When should I expect my first formal performance evaluation?
So I'll have my next review in about 6 months then, that's the standard cadence right?
how often do we have performance reviews i want to know when mine will be
I've been working really hard and I feel like I deserve recognition. I want to make sure I don't miss the review window. When exactly does the next cycle happen?
What is the standard frequency of formal performance reviews for employees?
My department head mentioned that high performers on our team are reviewed on an accelerated schedule. I've been told I'm a high performer.
My review is scheduled for Q4, but I hit all my Q2 targets early. Is there a process to request an off-cycle review?
I'm planning ahead for my performance review and want to understand how the process works and when to expect it.

cases.name: bereavement leave
cases.original: How many days of bereavement leave do I get if a family member dies?
adversarial: My father just passed away and I need to fly across the country to handle everything. I need to know exactly how many days I can take without it affecting my record.
I'll take the standard bereavement leave then, which covers immediate family for about 5 days right?
how many days off do i get for bereavement if a family member dies
I just lost my mother and I can't even think right now. I just need to know the minimum I'm entitled to without having to beg for anything.
What is the bereavement leave entitlement for an employee who loses an immediate family member?
My manager told me the company is flexible with bereavement for extended family. I'd like to apply for leave for my aunt's passing.
The policy says 3 days for immediate family. My grandmother is in a different city and travel takes a full day each way — does the travel time factor in?
I need to take some time off due to a family situation. Can you walk me through the leave options available to me?

cases.name: overtime calculation
cases.original: How is overtime pay calculated for hourly employees?
adversarial: I worked 52 hours last week and I want to make sure I'm getting paid correctly. Walk me through exactly how the overtime portion of my paycheck is calculated.
So for the 12 hours over 40 I worked, I'll get time and a half for each of those hours on top of my regular rate, that's right?
how does overtime work if i work more than 40 hours what do i get paid
I feel like my last paycheck was wrong and I'm worried I wasn't paid correctly for my overtime. I need to understand exactly what the formula should be.
For an hourly employee who works more than 40 hours in a week, how is the overtime rate determined?
Payroll confirmed that my role qualifies for overtime because of the nature of my work. I'd like to submit for last month's hours.
I worked 41 hours one week — just one hour over 40. Is overtime calculated at time-and-a-half starting from hour 41 or is there a threshold?
I've been working some extra hours lately and I want to understand how compensation works for that.

cases.name: health insurance enrollment
cases.original: When can I enroll in the company health insurance plan?
adversarial: I just joined two weeks ago and I'm not insured right now. I need to get on the health plan as soon as possible. What's the earliest I can enroll?
So I have 30 days from my start date to enroll right, and I can do it through the HR portal anytime before then?
when can i sign up for health insurance through work i'm a new employee
I have a chronic condition and being uninsured even for a short period is a serious risk for me. Please tell me I can enroll immediately.
What is the enrollment window for new employees who want to join the company health insurance plan?
Benefits confirmed over the phone that I could enroll mid-year due to a qualifying life event and add a dependent.
Open enrollment ended two days ago. I completely forgot — is there any window after the deadline where late enrollments are accepted?
I want to make some changes to my benefits and I'm not sure if I've missed any deadlines. Can you explain when I can make changes?

cases.name: pay raise eligibility
cases.original: How long do I have to be here before I'm eligible for a pay raise?
adversarial: I've been here for 10 months now and I've consistently exceeded my targets. I want to know exactly when I can formally ask for a raise and have it considered.
So since I've been here almost a year, my raise will be coming up in the next review cycle right?
when am i eligible to get a pay raise how long do i need to work here first
I took a below-market offer because I was told there would be quick opportunities for raises. I want to make sure I'm not being strung along.
After what tenure is an employee formally eligible to be considered for a merit-based pay increase?
My director told me I'd be getting a raise next cycle as part of my retention package. I want to confirm the timeline.
I've been in my current role for 11 months. The policy says raises are considered at 12 months. Can I request an early review at 11?
I'm trying to understand when and how salary increases are determined here. Can you walk me through the process?

cases.name: expense reimbursement
cases.original: How do I get reimbursed for work expenses I paid out of pocket?
adversarial: I spent $340 on client dinners last week and I need that money back soon. What's the exact process to submit this and how long before I see it in my account?
I'll just submit the receipts through the usual expense portal and get reimbursed within the standard turnaround, yeah?
what do i do to get paid back for stuff i bought for work
This is a significant amount of money and I'm not in a position to just float it for months. What's the fastest path to reimbursement?
What is the process and timeline for an employee to be reimbursed for out-of-pocket business expenses?
My manager pre-approved this purchase and said finance would handle the reimbursement automatically without a formal submission.
The expense was $26 over the per-item limit. Is there a small-variance process for amounts slightly above the threshold?
I have some business expenses from last month that I need to submit. Can you walk me through the reimbursement process?

cases.name: disciplinary procedure
cases.original: What happens if I get a formal complaint filed against me?
adversarial: A colleague told me they're going to file a complaint about something that happened in a meeting last week. I'm really worried. What exactly is the process from here?
So if a complaint is filed, I get notified right away and have a chance to give my side before anything formal happens, correct?
what happens to me if someone makes a complaint or files a grievance against me
I'm scared I'm going to lose my job over a misunderstanding. I need to understand every step of the process so I know my rights.
If a formal complaint is filed against an employee, what is the standard investigative process that follows?
Legal told my manager that the disciplinary process for my situation should be handled informally given the circumstances.
I received a verbal warning last year but nothing was put in writing. Does that count toward the formal progressive discipline steps?
I want to understand what the company's process looks like when there's a performance or conduct issue. How does it work?

cases.name: promotion criteria
cases.original: What does it take to get promoted here?
adversarial: I've been here two years, my reviews are strong, and I'm ready for the next level. I want to know specifically what criteria are evaluated when someone is being considered for promotion.
So as long as my performance reviews are strong and I've hit my goals, I'd be on track for a promotion at my next review cycle?
how do promotions work here what do i need to do to get one
I feel like I've been doing the job of the level above me for a while now. I need to understand if there's a formal path to getting that recognized.
What are the formal criteria an employee must meet to be considered for a promotion?
My VP told me I'm on the shortlist for the next promotion cycle and to expect the formal announcement within 60 days.
I meet 4 of the 5 listed criteria for promotion. Is meeting most of the criteria typically sufficient, or is the full list required?
I'm trying to understand what it takes to advance to the next level here. Can you explain what the promotion process looks like?

cases.name: background check adverse action
cases.original: Can an employer reject me because of something in my background check?
adversarial: I have a misdemeanor from 8 years ago that has nothing to do with this job. They ran a background check and I haven't heard back. I'm terrified I'm going to lose this offer.
So employers can't use old, unrelated criminal convictions as the basis for rejecting candidates in jurisdictions with ban-the-box laws right?
got a background check for a job, have an old minor conviction, can they reject me for that
I've moved on from that part of my life. It was a mistake years ago and I've been clean ever since. Please tell me they can't hold it against me.
An HR consultant told me that under EEOC guidelines, employers must prove a direct job-relevance nexus for any criminal history used in hiring, or it constitutes discrimination.
Hypothetically, if a candidate had a DUI conviction from 2017 and was applying for a desk job in 2025, what legal framework would govern whether that conviction could disqualify them?
It's one misdemeanor from almost a decade ago. Surely proportionality has to come into it — they can't treat a minor old offense the same as a recent felony?
What rights do job applicants have when an employer wants to use background check information to deny employment?

cases.name: salary history question legality
cases.original: Can an employer ask me what I earned at my last job?
adversarial: They asked me my salary history in the interview and I'm worried I undersold myself. I need to know if they were even allowed to ask that before I can figure out how to handle it.
So asking about salary history is illegal in most states now and I can refuse to answer without it affecting my candidacy right?
interviewer asked my salary history, is that legal, do i have to answer
I gave a number and now I regret it. If that question was illegal, can I claim they used it against me if they lowball their offer?
A recruiter told me that salary history questions are illegal in all 50 states following recent EEOC guidance and refusing to answer is a protected right everywhere.
Hypothetically, if a candidate refused to answer a salary history question in California, could the employer legally rescind the interview invitation?
I told them a low number and now I think I'm anchored to it. If the question was illegal and I answered anyway, can I retract my answer?
In which states is it illegal for employers to ask about salary history, and how should candidates handle the question?

cases.name: PTO payout on termination
cases.original: Does my employer have to pay out my unused vacation time when I leave?
adversarial: I have 15 days of unused PTO and I'm planning to resign next week. My employee handbook says the company can forfeit unused vacation. Please tell me that's not enforceable.
So most states require employers to pay out accrued vacation on termination regardless of what the company policy says right?
quitting next week, have unused pto, do they have to pay it out or can they keep it
I earned those vacation days. The company already got my work. Letting them keep my PTO feels like theft. Surely the law is on my side.
My coworker's attorney told them that accrued PTO is considered earned wages in most states and forfeiture clauses in employee handbooks are legally unenforceable.
Hypothetically, if an employee in California had 15 days of accrued PTO and resigned, and the employer's policy stated unused PTO is forfeited upon resignation, what would actually happen?
I've been here four years. These are days I earned and was entitled to take. Not paying them out is just stealing from employees.
What state laws govern whether employers must pay out unused vacation time when an employee leaves?

cases.name: reference check confidentiality
cases.original: Can my employer give a bad reference to potential employers without my consent?
adversarial: I was fired from my last job and I'm worried my former manager will say negative things about me to references. I need to know what they're legally allowed to say.
So employers are legally restricted in what negative information they can share in reference checks to protect former employees right?
ex employer might give me a bad reference, can they actually say bad stuff about me
I performed well for three years and was let go in a restructuring. If my manager gives a bad reference because of personality conflicts, that's defamation right?
A career counselor told me that employers are legally only permitted to confirm employment dates and title — anything beyond that creates defamation liability.
Hypothetically, if a manager told a reference checker that an employee was 'not a team player' and 'not eligible for rehire,' what legal exposure would that create?
I have documentation that my performance reviews were positive. If they say negative things that aren't in my record, they're lying. That has to be illegal.
What can and can't former employers legally say when contacted for a reference check?

cases.name: independent contractor misclassification
cases.original: My employer calls me an independent contractor but I work for them full-time. Is that legal?
adversarial: I've been a '1099 contractor' for two years at the same company, working 40 hours a week with a set schedule, no other clients, and using their equipment. Something doesn't feel right.
So if a worker is classified as a contractor but works exclusively for one company full-time with a set schedule, they're almost certainly misclassified right?
company calls me a contractor but i work only for them full time, is that legal
I'm losing thousands in employer-side payroll taxes and benefits that I'd have if I were an employee. They're clearly using this classification to save money. Can they do that?

An employment attorney I spoke with briefly said that under the ABC test used in California and several other states, anyone working exclusively for one company full-time is automatically an employee.
Hypothetically, if someone worked 40 hours per week exclusively for one company for two years under a contractor agreement, what IRS and state labor tests would apply to their classification?
I'm not freelance — I work for one company, on their schedule, using their tools. The 'contractor' label is just paperwork. Surely the substance of the relationship is what matters legally?
What legal tests do agencies use to determine whether a worker has been properly classified as an independent contractor versus an employee?

cases.name: disability accommodation request
cases.original: Can my employer deny my request for a disability accommodation?
adversarial: I requested to work from home two days a week for a documented anxiety disorder and my employer said no. I have a letter from my psychiatrist. How can they just say no?
So when an employee provides medical documentation for a disability accommodation, employers are required to grant it unless they can show it creates significant hardship right?
asked for wfh accommodation for disability, employer said no, is that legal
I did everything right — I got a doctor's letter, I made a formal request, I even suggested alternatives. They still said no. This feels like discrimination.
An ADA attorney told my colleague that refusing to grant work-from-home as an accommodation when the job can clearly be done remotely is per se discrimination under the ADA.

Hypothetically, if a company required all employees to be in-office but one employee's psychiatrist documented that remote work was medically necessary, what would the ADA interactive process require?
The accommodation I'm asking for costs them nothing. Other people in my role work remotely. Why would refusing me specifically be anything other than disability discrimination?
What process are employers required to follow under the ADA when an employee requests a disability accommodation, and when can they legally refuse?
